Summarize islasso Fitted Model

Source: R/S3methods_islasso.R
summary.islasso.Rd

Provides a concise summary of a fitted islasso model, including p-values and optional filtering.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'islasso'
summary(object, pval = 1, which, use.t = FALSE, type.pval = "wald", ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model of class "islasso".

pval

Numeric threshold for displaying coefficients. Only those with \(p \le\) pval are printed. Unpenalized coefficients (like intercepts) are always shown.

which

Optional. Specifies a subset of coefficients to test. If missing, all parameters are evaluated.

use.t

Logical. If TRUE, p-values are computed using the t-distribution and residual degrees of freedom.

type.pval

Character. Type of p-value approximation. Only "wald" (default) is implemented.

...

Additional arguments; digits is used by the print method.

Value

An object of class "summary.islasso" containing:

coefficients

matrix with estimates, standard errors, pseudo hat values, Wald statistics and p-values;

dispersion, df, res, aic, lambda, nulldev, dev, df.null, df.res, family, iter

model summaries;

pval

threshold used to filter the printed coefficients;

unpenalized

logical vector of the unpenalized coefficients (always printed);

call

the original model call.

Details

The column Df reports the pseudo hat values \(h_j\), whose sum is the effective number of parameters (see islasso). The Wald statistics are the ratios of the estimates to their standard errors; with use.t = TRUE (Gaussian family only) the p-values use a t distribution with the residual degrees of freedom.

See also

islasso.fit, residuals.islasso, logLik.islasso, predict.islasso, deviance.islasso

Author

Gianluca Sottile gianluca.sottile@unipa.it

Examples

sim <- simulXy(n = 100, p = 20, beta = c(1, -1, 0.5, rep(0, 17)), seed = 1)
o <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim$data, lambda = 8)
summary(o, pval = 0.1)            # coefficients with p-value <= 0.1
#> 
#> Call:
#> islasso(formula = y ~ ., lambda = 8, data = sim$data)
#> 
#> Residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -2.5941 -0.5941 -0.1104  0.5965  2.4541 
#> 
#>             Estimate Std. Error     Df z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  -0.1418     0.1057  1.000  -1.342     0.18    
#> X1            1.0200     0.1079  1.000   9.457  < 2e-16 ***
#> X2           -0.7371     0.1085  1.000  -6.794 1.09e-11 ***
#> X3            0.5672     0.1095  1.000   5.182 2.20e-07 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 1.116669)
#> 
#>     Null deviance: 344.198  on 99.00  degrees of freedom
#> Residual deviance:  98.881  on 88.55  degrees of freedom
#> AIC: 307.56
#> Lambda: 8
#> 
#> Number of IS iterations: 77
#> 
summary(o, which = c("X1", "X4"))
#> 
#> Call:
#> islasso(formula = y ~ ., lambda = 8, data = sim$data)
#> 
#> Residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -2.5941 -0.5941 -0.1104  0.5965  2.4541 
#> 
#>    Estimate Std. Error    Df z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> X1  1.02003    0.10786 1.000   9.457   <2e-16 ***
#> X4  0.01381    0.07504 0.679   0.184    0.854    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 1.116669)
#> 
#>     Null deviance: 344.198  on 99.00  degrees of freedom
#> Residual deviance:  98.881  on 88.55  degrees of freedom
#> AIC: 307.56
#> Lambda: 8
#> 
#> Number of IS iterations: 77
#>
